title: Simplification & Algebra
shortDescription: BODMAS order of operations plus the handful of algebraic identities that turn 'find the value' questions into one-line answers.
genZNote: BODMAS's D-before-M placement in the acronym is a total mind trick. Division and multiplication are ride-or-die equals, left to right — no hierarchy between them at all.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: Simplification is about applying one consistent order of operations correctly under time pressure; Algebra (at this exam's level) is mostly about recognising when a 'find the value' expression is secretly one of a handful of standard identities — which skips solving for individual variables entirely.

sections.heading: BODMAS — the Real Rule
sections.body: Brackets, Of (multiplication expressed as 'of', e.g. ½ of 20), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. The order in the acronym does NOT mean division always happens before multiplication, or addition always before subtraction — those two pairs are EQUAL precedence, evaluated strictly left to right in whichever order they appear in the expression.
bullets: Example: 20 ÷ 4 × 2 = (20÷4) × 2 = 5 × 2 = 10 — NOT 20 ÷ (4×2) = 2.5. Left to right, not 'multiplication before division'.

sections.heading: Recognising an Identity in Disguise — Fast Method

steps.name: Standard method
steps.explanation: Given x + 1/x = 5, find x² + 1/x². The slow route: solve the quadratic x² − 5x + 1 = 0 for x, then square and add the reciprocal.
steps.purpose: Works, but involves solving a quadratic and handling irrational roots.

steps.name: Fast exam method
steps.explanation: Square both sides directly: (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23.
steps.purpose: One line, no quadratic, no individual value of x ever needed.

sections.heading: Never Solve for Individual Variables Unless Asked
sections.body: If a question gives you a+b and ab, and asks for a²+b², you do NOT need to find a and b individually. Use a²+b² = (a+b)² − 2ab directly. This single habit — checking whether the question only needs a combined expression rather than the individual variables — is the single biggest time-saver in exam Algebra.

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Treating BODMAS's D-before-M as an actual precedence rule — they're equal, left to right.
Solving a full system of equations for individual variables when the question only asks for a combined expression an identity gives directly.
Sign errors when expanding (a−b)² or (a−b)³ — the alternating signs are easy to drop under time pressure; write out the full expansion once on scratch paper if unsure.

sections.heading: Exam Strategy
bullets: Scan any 'find the value' Algebra question for a matching identity before starting any expansion by hand.

In multi-operation Simplification expressions, resolve brackets fully first, then move strictly left to right through the remaining operators respecting only Brackets > Of > (Division/Multiplication, left to right) > (Addition/Subtraction, left to right).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Simplification applies one strict left-to-right order of operations (BODMAS); exam Algebra is mostly spotting standard identities to skip solving for individual variables.
keyFacts: Division and multiplication are equal precedence, left to right — same for addition and subtraction.
x² + 1/x² from x + 1/x: square both sides, then subtract 2.
commonConfusion: BODMAS's letter order is not a strict precedence ladder for D/M and A/S — those pairs tie, and ties resolve left to right.

highYieldFacts: (a+b)² − (a−b)² = 4ab is a fast route to 'find ab given a+b and a−b'.
Squaring x + 1/x (or x − 1/x) and subtracting/adding 2 is the standard fast route to x² + 1/x².
commonTraps: Applying D-before-M or A-before-S as strict precedence instead of left-to-right equal precedence.
Expanding a system fully to find individual variables when only a combined expression is asked.
mustRemember: a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b) is the single most reused identity for fast factorisation.
